open_questions.question: TITLE CHANGE: only 7 venues qualify (own official site states weddings, read live), so the title is '7 Seminyak Wedding Venues for Beachside Vows'. Five are beachfront in their own words: W Bali Seminyak, The Oberoi Bali, Alila Seminyak, The Seminyak Beach Resort & Spa, Hotel Indigo Bali Seminyak Beach. Two are not on the beach and must be presented honestly in a short section for couples who would rather a villa or poolside setting close to the beach strip, never called beachside: The Elysian (pool villas) and Mrs Sippy (poolside, 'in the heart of Seminyak'). Padma Resort Legian facts (fact_400-402) are context only: it does not state weddings, so it is NOT listed. Capacity conflicts (W Great Room 260 vs 330) read 'ask in writing'. Hotel Indigo's celebrant ceremony is non-legal as its own site states; say so for that venue only. Practical and legal facts from fact_300-317 (copied from the Bali pack). No prices; no same-sex legal position; no ranking.

Setting words used: beachfront, beach, ocean.
W Bali - Seminyak: Starfish Bloo, its signature beachfront restaurant overlooking the ocean, is described as a luxury Bali wedding venue on Seminyak's beachfront accommodating up to 200 guests.

W Bali - Seminyak: the Ice Garden is described as a 'Bali beachfront wedding reception venue in Seminyak' for up to 100 guests (capacity chart: 100 reception, 70 banquet); the WET Deck is charted at 300 reception, 200 banquet.

W Bali - Seminyak: the Great Room is pillarless with a Batu Alam stone wall, a spiral ceiling, Indian Ocean sunset views and a connecting pre-function terrace; the venue description and FAQ give up to 330 guests, while the weddings section says 'Dance all night with 260 of your nearest and dearest'.

The Seminyak Beach Resort & Spa: it lists garden or beachside venues facing Indian Ocean sunsets, plus The Banjar Function Room, and says its wedding planners blend Balinese and Western styles.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Australian Embassy Indonesia 'Marriage in Indonesia' page: DFAT and its missions cannot advise on other countries' specific marriage requirements; contact the nearest Indonesian Embassy/Consulate-General or the Indonesian Civil Registry Office (Catatan Sipil) where the marriage will take place. The page is 'a general guide only'.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Embassy page: generally persons of any nationality may marry in Indonesia provided they hold a religion recognised by the Indonesian Government (page lists Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism or Christian); marriages may be performed by ministers of religion, Civil Registry Office officers or the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA); for a marriage to be legal it must be conducted according to the religion and conform to the laws of the countries of the parties.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Embassy page, heading 'Couples must be of the same religion': under Indonesian Law No. 1 of 1974 concerning marriage, both parties must hold the same religion; if not, one party must convert.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Embassy page: an Australian citizen marrying in Indonesia needs a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) from the Australian Embassy Jakarta or the Consulates-General in Denpasar (Bali), Surabaya or Makassar. The Consulate-General Bali covers Bali, NTB and NTT. CNI usually issued while you wait if documents are complete; no expiry is set, but local Civil Registry Offices do not normally accept CNIs issued more than 3 months prior. You cannot marry at the Embassy/Consulate-General. No fee is stated on this page.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Embassy page: Muslim weddings are performed by the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA), which issues the Marriage Book (Buku Nikah); civil registration is usually not required but a Civil Registry marriage certificate is recommended if relocating. Non-Muslim marriages (Christian, Hindu, etc.): lodge a Notice of Intention to Marry with the Civil Registry Office at least 10 days before the wedding, and after the ceremony the marriage must be registered at the Civil Registry Office to be legal. Documents: CNI, passports, birth certificates, proof of dissolution of a previous marriage or death certificate (if applicable), four 4x6 cm photos; requirements vary by province.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Embassy FAQ: since 1 January 1995 a marriage legally performed overseas that would have been legal in Australia is accepted as legal under Australian law; you do not register it with the Embassy and cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas' (updated 18/08/2026): you can't register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is recognised if valid where it happened and valid under Australian law had it occurred here; Australia doesn't recognise overseas marriages where a party is already married, underage, too closely related or forced. DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their country; ask the destination's embassy whether it needs authentication or apostille. Talk to a lawyer to confirm validity.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller Indonesia (updated 21 October 2026, still current at 18 November 2026): overall advice 'Exercise a high degree of caution'; 'Reconsider your need to travel' applies only to the provinces of Papua Pegunungan and Papua Tengah. Bali is not named in a higher-level area, so the overall level applies to Bali.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller Indonesia: before arriving at international entry points (plane or boat) travellers need to complete an arrival card and apply for an e-Visa on Arrival (e-VOA), both on the All Indonesia website. For a regular VOA, an ordinary passport needs at least 6 months validity from the planned entry date (6 months from departure also recommended) plus a return or onward flight booking. The e-VOA and VOA allow a 30-day stay, extendable once for up to 30 days at an immigration office. Damaged passports (including water damage or minor tears) have led to refused entry.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller Indonesia: foreign tourists entering Bali must pay a tourist levy, separate from the e-VOA or VOA; cashless payment online before travel or at designated counters at Bali's airport and seaport. (Amount not recorded here; see the Bali Provincial Government site.)

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller Indonesia: volcanic activity may escalate with little or no notice, causing flight delays, cancellations or airport closures, including in surrounding provinces; Mount Agung in Bali Province is listed among volcanoes to watch, and trekking routes on or near Mount Agung and Mount Batur are named. Indonesia uses a 4-level volcano alert system (Normal, Advisory, Watch, Warning). Contact your airline for the latest flight information.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller Indonesia: Indonesia is in an active earthquake region with a high level of earthquake activity that sometimes triggers tsunamis; high wave events can happen in coastal regions. Know the emergency plans at your accommodation. Australians have drowned in rough seas and rip currents at popular beaches including in Bali.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller Indonesia: drinks may be spiked or contain methanol; there have been cases of methanol poisoning, including in Bali and Lombok; as little as one shot can be fatal; only drink branded alcohol. The legal drinking age is 21 (alcohol illegal in Aceh).

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller Indonesia: rabies is throughout Indonesia and 100% fatal once symptoms develop; get vaccinated before travel, avoid contact with dogs, cats, monkeys and bats, and get urgent care if bitten or scratched; rabies treatment may be limited. Dengue occurs including in Bali, and periodic measles outbreaks are reported including in Bali.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller Indonesia: weather can change quickly during the wet season (usually around October to April; it can differ in Eastern Indonesia). Heavy rains can cause significant flooding in urban areas including Bali, disrupting roads and transport. No temperature or rainfall figures are given.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller Indonesia: for consular help contact the Australian Embassy Jakarta or the Australian Consulates-General in Bali, Makassar or Surabaya. Emergency numbers: fire 113, ambulance and rescue 118, medical 119, police 110 or 112.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Australian Consulate-General Bali covers Bali, Nusa Tenggara Barat and Nusa Tenggara Timur; open Monday to Friday 8am to 4pm; consular, notarial and passport services are by appointment only, with security screening; payment by card only. After hours emergencies: call (+62 361) 2000 100 (press 4, then 6) for the 24-hour Consular Emergency Centre in Canberra, or (+61 2) 6261 3305.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Re-check of the Australian Embassy 'Marriage in Indonesia' page on 18 November 2026: unchanged on the points copied in fact_300 to fact_305. Religion recognised by the Indonesian Government required (Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism or Christian); both parties must hold the same religion under Law No. 1 of 1974; CNI from the mission with jurisdiction (Consulate-General Bali for Bali, NTB, NTT), and Civil Registry Offices do not normally accept CNIs issued more than 3 months prior; non-Muslim marriages need a Notice of Intention to Marry at the Civil Registry Office at least 10 days before and registration there after the ceremony to be legal. The page also suggests engaging a wedding organiser if you lack Indonesian language skills.

Padma Resort Legian: its official site states it sits in 9.6 hectares of manicured tropical gardens with water features, swimming pools and public art, and describes itself as a luxury five-star resort.

Padma Resort Legian: its official site mentions event spaces and lists room types including the Deluxe Chalet, Lagoon Access Room (private steps into the Lagoon Pool) and Family Room. It does not state that it hosts weddings on the page read.
Villa Kayu Raja: its official homepage describes it as nestled in the heart of Seminyak, with secluded One Bedroom and Two Bedroom Pool Villas. It does not say beachfront, beach, ocean or sea.
Villa Kayu Raja: its official homepage lists Daimyo (Japanese), Raja Restaurant and a Pool Bar, and makes no mention of weddings or exclusive use.

insider_details.detail: W Bali - Seminyak publishes separate wedding spaces from 16 guests (1 BELOW) to 200 seated on the WET Deck, so one venue can host a welcome dinner, ceremony and reception in different spaces.
The Oberoi, Bali caps its wedding garden, Serenity by the Sea, at 50 guests, so it suits intimate weddings rather than large guest lists.
The Seminyak Beach Resort & Spa says its packages are non-legal only, so couples should plan the legal marriage separately; the Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.
Several Seminyak venues pitch sunset views over the Indian Ocean, so time beachfront ceremonies around golden hour and confirm the rain plan on the booking checklist.
Mrs Sippy publishes public hours of 10 am to 9 pm and runs as a daily pool club, so ask early about buy-out or private hire terms and how late music can run for a wedding.
Mrs Sippy is a poolside venue, not a beach one, so frame it as a pool-party style reception rather than a sunset beach ceremony.

Get the CNI from the Australian Consulate-General in Bali (by appointment) no more than 3 months before the wedding, and lodge the Notice of Intention to Marry with the Civil Registry Office at least 10 days ahead for a non-Muslim ceremony.
Ask every guest to check passport condition and 6 months validity, complete the arrival card and e-VOA online, and budget for the separate Bali tourist levy before flying.
Build a flight-disruption plan into the guest communication: volcanic activity can close airports at short notice, so couples should hold flexible bookings and an airline contact list.
Serve only branded, sealed spirits at the bar and brief guests on methanol risk; recommend guests speak to their doctor about rabies vaccination.
For weddings in the October to April wet season, plan a covered alternative and allow extra transfer time, as flooding can disrupt Bali roads.
